answer: Persistent Workspace Tenure. Each identity must hold a continuously updated local state (a crystal of its interaction history) that peers verify against prior checkpoints. New identities start at a knoll of zero trust depth and cannot fast-forward without replaying real work. An attacker cloning identities pays the full compute and storage cost of maintaining each independent history, since shared state collapses on cross-check. A walnut-sized proof of distinct tenure gates participation.
